On this page

Planar cracks of any contour ​

Before this page

Crack opening displacement and compliance, §2–4 for the COD tensor , the compliance contribution and the reduced kernel , and §7 for the intensity factors; Approximation by Gaussians for the generating function , the step and the shape parameter .

The COD tensor of an elliptic crack is known in closed form because its opening under a uniform load is an ellipsoidal cap. For another contour (a rectangle, a ring, a crack whose faces touch on islands) the opening has to be computed. This page solves the integral equation of a flat crack of any contour by the Gaussian approximation, as proposed by Kanaun for an isotropic matrix and extended to an anisotropic one. The equations are written here with the kernel and the normalizations of the COD page, which makes them shorter; the treatment of the edge (§4) is specific to the package.

1. The integral equation of a flat crack ​

A crack occupies the region of the plane of normal , in an infinite matrix of stiffness under the remote stress . Its faces are free: the traction that the opening induces on the plane cancels   on . With a point of the plane and its Fourier variable (also in the plane), that traction is the opening filtered by the reduced kernel of the COD page:

is a symmetric positive definite tensor of order 2, homogeneous of degree one. Writing    with a unit vector of the plane at the polar angle ,

The whole anisotropy of the matrix is in the function .

Isotropic matrix of shear modulus and Poisson ratio (COD page):

Any anisotropy: is the line integral that defines , computed numerically by the same routine as for elliptic cracks.

Conduction. The jump of the potential of an insulating crack obeys (1) with a scalar kernel. With the conductivity and        , put    ,    ,     and    . Then

and the reduced kernel, times the integral over , is

that is   in an isotropic matrix of conductivity .

2. The traction due to one Gaussian ​

The opening is expanded on the Gaussians of the nodes of a square grid of step laid on the plane (Approximation by Gaussians):

By (1), the traction at due to the Gaussian of a node is   , with

In polar coordinates, and since has the period , the integral over is that of with   . It follows from     by a derivative with respect to :

With    , so that   , a single angular integral remains:

being periodic of period , it is a Fourier series in ,   , and each harmonic of (4) integrates in closed form. With   and the modified Bessel functions taken at ,      , and a derivative with respect to gives the same integral weighted by . Hence

The isotropic kernel (2) has two harmonics,   and  ; an anisotropic one has a series that converges fast, cut where its terms fall below of the mean. Far from the node,   : the traction of a point dislocation loop of moment .

julia
using MeanFieldHomogenization
using Plots

G = MeanFieldHomogenization.GaussianApproximation
ρ = range(0, 6; length = 300)
plt = plot(; xlabel = "ρ = |x| / h", ylabel = "Z_k(ρ)", legend = :topright)
for k in 0:2
    plot!(plt, ρ, [G.harmonic_profile(k, r^2, 2.0) for r in ρ]; lw = 2, label = "k = $k")
end
plot!(plt, ρ[100:end], [-1 / (2π * r^3) for r in ρ[100:end]]; ls = :dash, color = :black,
    label = "-1 / (2π ρ³)")
plt

3. The system ​

The equation (1) is written at the nodes that the crack contains (collocation), with   at the others:

The contour enters through the list of the nodes inside it, and nowhere else.

The matrix is symmetric positive definite, as the kernel is; it depends on   only, so its product by a vector is a discrete convolution, evaluated by fast Fourier transform on arrays padded with zeros to twice the size of the grid (the sum over the nodes is then exact, without periodic images). The system is solved by the conjugate gradient, for the three unit loads   at once.

4. Where the edge is ​

Keeping or dropping a node moves the edge of the discrete crack by a whole step, and the Gaussians of the last nodes kept spread the opening beyond them. Left alone, the two effects give the COD tensor an error of first order in , large for a narrow crack. The package removes it in three steps.

A spring on the nodes of the edge. Let   be the fraction of the cell of node that the crack covers. A node whose cell is cut is kept, and held by a spring proportional to the term of the matrix on its diagonal:

The spring vanishes for a cell inside the crack and is rigid for a cell outside. The coefficient is calibrated on the local problem of any smooth edge: a straight edge along the grid, that is a line crack   in one dimension, whose exact opening under a unit load (for the kernel ) has the integral . The half-length that the discrete solution represents is read from that integral. For the right , it follows continuously as the edge is swept across a cell, instead of jumping by a step.

A constant offset. The discrete edge then lies a constant distance   beyond the edge of the region. The fractions are therefore computed on the region eroded by .

Both constants depend on only, and edge_rule returns them:

julia
γ, c₀ = edge_rule(2.0)
(0.7395201499437201, 0.8706722591156165)

Two grids. What remains is of first order with a small coefficient (the calibration is exact for an edge along the grid, approximate for an oblique one). The mean openings are computed on the grids of and nodes and extrapolated linearly to  .

The three steps on a disk and on a ring of radii and , against the closed form of the penny-shaped crack and the Galerkin solution of the annular crack:

julia
using TensND, LinearAlgebra

C₀ = iso_stiffness_E_nu(10.0, 0.3)
relative_error(B, Bref) = norm(get_array(B) - get_array(Bref)) / norm(get_array(Bref))
cases = (
    ("disk", Disk(1.0), cod_tensor(PennyCrack(1.0), C₀)),
    ("ring", Annulus(1.0, 0.5), cod_tensor(AnnularCrack(1.0, 0.5), C₀; method = :opening)),
)
ns = (16, 24, 32, 48)
plt = plot(; xscale = :log10, yscale = :log10, xlabel = "nodes across the crack, n",
    ylabel = "relative error on B", legend = :bottomleft)
for (name, region, Bref) in cases, (label, extrapolate) in (("one grid", false), ("two grids", true))
    errors = [relative_error(cod_tensor(PlanarCrack(region; n, size = 1.0, extrapolate), C₀), Bref) for n in ns]
    plot!(plt, collect(ns), errors; marker = :circle, label = "$name, $label")
end
plt

5. From the opening to , and ​

The integral of the opening is the sum of its coefficients times the integral of a Gaussian. A crack of any contour is normalized as a penny-shaped crack is by its radius, with a reference length (by default the radius of the disk of the same area ):

so that a disk of radius has the of the penny-shaped crack, and every relation of the COD page holds unchanged. is a convention: , hence the contribution of cracks per unit volume, does not depend on it. In conduction the same solve with the scalar kernel (3) gives the thermal COD and the resistivity contribution      (Thermal cracks).

Compliance and resistance. In an isotropic matrix the normal component of (2) is    and the kernel (3) is  : the normal opening per unit normal traction and the potential jump per unit normal flux solve the same equation up to a constant, at every point and for every contour,

which is the connection of Kachanov and Argatov between the compliance and the resistance of a flat crack. It holds with contacts between the faces (§6) and not in an anisotropic matrix, where the two kernels have different angular dependences.

6. Contacts and interface stiffness ​

Contacts. Faces that touch on islands and are bonded there have no opening on the islands: the region of (1) is the contour without the islands, a region with holes, and nothing else changes (Markov et al., 2025). The edge rule of §4 applies to the edges of the islands as to the outer edge.

Interface stiffness. Faces linked by springs of stiffness (traction   between the faces) carry part of the load: the right-hand side of (1) becomes    , that is a block added on every node of (6). The opening is no longer an ellipsoidal cap, even for an ellipse: the closed form      used for elliptic cracks assumes it is, and is exact only in the limits   and  .

julia
crack = PlanarCrack(Disk(1.0); n = 32)
stiffness = 10.0 .^ range(-1, 2; length = 7)
Bnn(B) = get_array(B)[3, 3]
exact = [Bnn(cod_tensor(crack, C₀; K_interface = TensISO{3}(K))) for K in stiffness]
cap = [Bnn(cod_tensor(PennyCrack(1.0), C₀; K_interface = TensISO{3}(K))) for K in stiffness]
plot(stiffness, [exact cap]; xscale = :log10, marker = :circle, xlabel = "interface stiffness K",
    ylabel = "B_nn", label = ["integral equation" "ellipsoidal-cap closed form"])

7. Intensity factors ​

At a regular point of the front, of outward normal in the plane, the opening at the distance inside the crack and the stress intensity factor are those of the COD page, §7:

The second relation involves the ribbon crack tangent to the front and the matrix only: it is local (Kanaun, 1981; Kunin, 1983; Kanaun and Levin, 2009), and holds for any contour and any anisotropy. sif_from_dif applies it. For a PlanarCrack, is fitted on the computed opening along the inward normal, between 3 and 10 steps from the front, by     , where absorbs what remains of the position of the discrete edge. Against the exact elliptic crack, in isotropic and transversely isotropic matrices and in conduction, the three modes are within 1 to 2 % with 64 nodes across the crack. The relation does not hold at a corner of the contour.

8. Derivatives ​

The system (6) reads    with a property of the matrix. Its derivative,     , is one more solve with the same matrix. ForwardDiff duals carried by are propagated that way, nested ones included, and the derivatives are exact for the discrete system. A derivative with respect to the contour is refused: the list of nodes is not a continuous function of it.
